findings.title: Materials' 128% earnings bet is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.31x forward but 39.47x trailing, a 56 percent compression that implies 128 percent earnings growth. That is the market underwriting a doubling of profits, a bet that looks stretched for a sector whose forward percentile sits at just 40.

findings.title: Health Care's 86% growth is a stretch
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple is only 3 percentile points below its trailing one, yet the implied earnings growth is 86 percent. The market is pricing in a massive earnings surge without much valuation discount, which is an aggressive assumption for a sector that just saw its forward percentile drop 26 points in a month.

findings.title: Communication Services' cheapness is a trap
findings.body: Communication Services sits at the 2nd percentile on forward P/E, yet its trailing percentile is 29, a 26-point gap that implies 57 percent earnings growth. The market is paying up for a recovery that has not shown up in reported earnings, and the forward percentile fell 18 points in a single week, suggesting fading confidence.
